event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Analog Devices, Inc. (ADI) continues to treat the COVID-19 pandemic as a live, multi-dimensional risk even though the first global outbreak occurred more than three years before the 21 November 2023 filing date.  Across the Risk Factors section the company reiterates that COVID-19 has already disrupted its workforce, manufacturing footprint and supply chain, and that it can still trigger further production delays, customer-payment problems and heightened exposure to other listed risks.  The disclosures are largely qualitative—no dollar figures or quantified capacity losses are supplied—but they expressly link the pandemic to operational, financial and logistical stress points such as factory access restrictions, supply-chain interruptions and customer demand volatility.  Most sentences rely on conditional language (“may,” “could”), signalling forward-looking uncertainty rather than certain impact; however ADI also acknowledges historic, realised disruption, which elevates severity.  Under the Time Decay Principle, COVID-19 qualifies as a recent event (≤ 3 years), so evidence that shows direct or ongoing impact can attain moderately high scores (7-8), while generic, boiler-plate mentions stay lower.  No strong mitigating statements (e.g., detailed contingency plans or quantified cost controls) are provided, so deductions are mainly for conditional phrasing rather than offsetting actions.
